newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen B shares close up on recent gains.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen B shares close up on recent gains.

text.p: Shenzhen's B share index ended sharply higher in heavy trading on Thursday, with institutions encouraged by the market's recent rises, brokers said.
The index rose 3.32 points or 2.05 percent to close at 165.53 with turnover expanding to HK$269.6 million from HK$146.2 million.
"Today's rise was a follow-up of Wednesday's solid performance," an analyst with Shenzhen J&A Securities Co said.
On Wednesday, the B share index gained 4.86 points or 3.09 percent to 162.20. Recent rises were linked to active foreign demand for the H shares issued by the Shenzhen Expressway Co, brokers said.
The road company listed in Hong Kong on Wednesday, closed on Thursday at HK$2.575 on heavy volume of 100.96 million shares compared with offer price of HK$2.20.
But the day's B share gains were capped by a drop in the A share market, which was dragged down by concerns that Beijing may adopt new anti-speculation measures, brokers said.
The A share index lost 3.18 points or 0.77 percent to 410.94 on turnover of 8.94 billion yuan, compared with Wednesday's 10.98 billion.
"B shares are likely to reverse their upward trend if A shares continue to drop," an analyst with China Southern Securities Co said.
"We already saw heavy selling orders placed by foreign investors on Thursday," the analyst said.
On the B share market, television tube maker Shenzhen SEG Co was the biggest gainer and jumped HK$0.51 or 7.23 percent to HK$7.56 on volume of 2.97 million shares.
Chiwan Petroleum Supply Base, the most active issue, climbed HK$0.11 to HK$4.87 as 4.41 million shares changed hands.
Textile firm Hainan Haide was the poorest performer on the A share market, falling 0.73 yuan or 9.40 percent to 7.04 yuan, with volume reaching 12.9 million shares after recent sharp rises.
